name: Qing dynasty
region: China under Qing rule; Manchu/Han and regional/status distinctions matter
summary: Court dress and visual culture are highly regulated in elite contexts; rank, gender, ethnicity, century and occasion materially change correct clothing.

wardrobe.text: chaofu and festival robes for appropriate formal court ranks
narrow sleeves and horse-hoof cuffs in formal Manchu-derived court dress

textiles_materials.text: silk satin, brocade, kesi tapestry and metallic-thread embroidery

hairstyle_headwear.text: hair/headwear must be sex, ethnicity, rank and century specific; never infer a queue merely from “Chinese”

architecture.text: palace/courtyard or urban settings by role

interior_furniture.text: screens, hardwood furniture, court furnishings as role-appropriate

food_drink_tableware.text: porcelain, lacquer and metal service objects

writing_calligraphy.text: Chinese and Manchu written contexts exist; visible text must be verified

ritual_custom.text: formal court robe iconography/rank is regulated and should not be assigned casually

lighting_technology.text: lamps, candles, lanterns; late-period scenes may require more specific research

incompatible_or_anachronistic.text: imperial five-clawed dragon symbols on an ordinary subject
Ming hairstyle copied into strict Qing court portrait

prompt_fragments.court: Treat rank markers as evidence-bearing choices, not decorative fantasy. If rank is unspecified, use non-imperial styling rather than borrowing imperial symbols.

sources.supports: chaofu form, Manchu adaptations and 1759 regulation
festival robe and reserved imperial symbols

scope_note: Foundation pack: use as a bounded starting point, not an encyclopedia.
strict_reconstruction_note: Strict court reconstruction requires date/reign, rank, gender, Manchu/Han context and occasion.
